firstSection.copytitle: Building the Web for everyone to use,with safety and accessibility in mind
firstSection.text:
I am currently deepening my understanding of cybersecurity while building on the practical experience I have gained through web development, including website implementation and improvement.
I believe a website does not create lasting value simply by being launched. Its quality and value depend on continued maintenance, operation, and improvement over time.
Building on my experience, I want to support websites over the long term by considering not only technical quality, but also usability and security from the perspective of the people who use them.

faq.question: What kind of experience do you have in web development?
faq.answer:
I have worked across a wide range of web-related projects, from backend development to website production.

Before 2016, I worked in backend development, where I was responsible for analyzing issues, identifying their root causes, and finding practical solutions.
In 2016, I transitioned to website development because I wanted to work not only on the underlying systems, but also on the user experience and visual aspects of websites.

faq.question: What were your responsibilities in website development?
faq.answer:
I handled website development, WordPress integration, deployment, and maintenance.

Based on design files created in Adobe Illustrator, I hand-coded websites from scratch, integrated them with WordPress, and handled the process through to deployment.
Working from requests and requirements provided by directors, I translated them into technical requirements, analyzed issues based on the site's structure, and proposed and implemented appropriate solutions.
As I was often the only person responsible for technical work, I also handled a wide range of technical matters beyond development, including maintenance, troubleshooting, and urgent issues.

faq.question: What do you focus on when designing and implementing websites?
faq.answer:
I focus on consistency across the entire site and long-term maintainability when designing and implementing websites.

Rather than simply building websites that are intuitive and easy to use, I try to understand the principles and rules behind both the design and implementation, and reflect them consistently throughout the site.
By organizing and structuring information, using semantic markup, and building reusable components and structures, I aim to create websites that are easier to maintain and improve over time.
Through my studies for the Web Design Skills Test, a national certification in Japan, I also developed an understanding of W3C web standards and WCAG principles.
I apply these concepts to my work by considering responsive design, cross-browser differences, and accessibility, with the goal of creating websites that are as accessible and usable as possible.

faq.question: What kinds of work did you take on to improve and maintain web quality after launch?
faq.answer:
After launch, I continued to work on improving and maintaining the quality of the websites I was responsible for.

Websites often develop a range of issues over time as content is updated and new features are added.
Rather than simply responding to day-to-day requests and routine tasks, I also proactively addressed issues I identified through ongoing operations and maintenance, including outdated code, inconsistencies across the site, semantic HTML structure, and accessibility.
I also reviewed company-specific frameworks and introduced tools that could be useful for specific tasks to improve the efficiency of routine work.

I also worked to make technical knowledge and solutions accessible to others rather than keeping them within individuals.
I introduced Slack so that past information could be searched and referenced, and organized frequently referenced information into documented rules and guidelines.
As a result, new directors were able to review past information on their own and proactively develop the knowledge they needed for their work.
When they encountered technical questions they could not resolve on their own, I provided guidance and explained what they needed to understand, supporting their learning according to their individual level of knowledge and experience.

Rather than simply addressing immediate problems, I made improvements with long-term maintainability, quality, and ease of day-to-day operations in mind.
Through this approach, I have worked to maintain and improve the quality of websites so that users can continue to use them with confidence.

  • ・Content updates and feature additions
  • ・WordPress and PHP version upgrades
  • ・Page speed improvements
  • ・Web accessibility improvements, including UI/UX
  • ・Refactoring and improving existing code
  • ・Improving the efficiency of routine tasks
  • ・Documenting and sharing technical information and solutions
  • ・Responding to technical questions and supporting others' learning

faq.question: What kinds of responsibilities did you handle outside of web production, particularly in the company's IT environment and other technical areas?
faq.answer:
In addition to web production, I took on a wide range of technical responsibilities as part of the company's internal IT function and also provided technical input on operational and business-related decisions.

I was responsible for a wide range of technical work supporting our web production environment, from setting up and configuring servers, databases, PHP, and development and testing environments to investigating issues and unexpected incidents and technically reviewing environments built by external contractors.
I was also consulted on server selection and on reviewing the plans and services offered to customers, and I provided technical input and proposals for company strategy meetings.

  • ・Selecting and setting up rental servers
  • ・Registering and configuring domains and subdomains
  • ・Installing and configuring databases and PHP
  • ・Setting up and configuring testing environments using XAMPP
  • ・Checking access logs and alerts when unexpected issues occurred
  • ・Researching related information and similar cases to form hypotheses and narrow down the cause
  • ・Contacting server providers when necessary
  • ・Providing technical support and answering questions from directors and junior staff
  • ・Reviewing environments built by external freelancers or the company president and making changes when necessary
  • ・Adding user accounts and tracking tags in response to customer requests

faq.question: Which industries have you worked with the most?
faq.answer:
My experience has primarily been in healthcare and social welfare, followed by manufacturing and construction.

The company I worked for had a background in healthcare consulting, so I was often involved in developing websites for hospitals.
I also frequently worked on projects related to social welfare, including web-based systems at a previous company.

faq.question: Which industry are you most passionate about?
faq.answer:
I have a particularly strong personal connection to the social welfare sector.

I grew up in an environment where my grandmother ran a jazz club that brought together people from many different backgrounds, including people with foreign roots and people with disabilities.
As a student, I spent a great deal of time with a classmate who was living with a mental illness and experiencing significant mental health difficulties, and who often used the school nurse’s office.
Through that experience, I came to know more people living with disabilities and other challenges in their daily lives.
I was later diagnosed with a developmental disability, and I also identify as non-binary.
As a result, I have become increasingly interested in learning about disability and gender, and I have made a point of reading books and seeking out information on my own.

Growing up around people from socially marginalized groups, I saw firsthand the circumstances they faced and how they were treated in society.
I have also experienced hardship and prejudice myself because of aspects of who I am that I cannot change.
I have often been approached by relatives and people I know for advice, and I have also had many opportunities to connect with people who, like me, live with disabilities or other challenges in their daily lives.
I have seen firsthand the difficulties and prejudice that people with disabilities can face in their everyday lives.
These experiences have led me to think deeply about how we can create environments where individual differences and perspectives are respected and where everyone can feel safe and comfortable interacting with others.
I have spent much of my life thinking about these questions and wrestling with how I can contribute.

Looking back on my life, I feel that the social welfare field is more deeply connected to my own experiences and the issues I care about than any other field.
That is why I want to use the perspective I have gained through my own lived experience and continue developing my technical skills so that I can help reduce, even in a small way, the hardships and prejudice faced by people who rely on social welfare services.

faq.question: What experience do you have in the social welfare field?
faq.answer:
I have used my IT knowledge and technical skills to support a wide range of work on my own in welfare-related environments.

Since I was a student, I have helped my grandmother with her business.
I handled a wide range of tasks, including administrative work, design support, macro development, PC repairs, and technical support.
I often worked independently and took care of whatever was needed on the IT side.
Through that experience, I was introduced to a friend of my grandmother who runs a disability welfare business.
I was asked to help there as well, and I supported a variety of work including administrative tasks, meetings, and web production.
I also handled a wide range of PC-related work.

In my previous job, I also worked on projects related to the social welfare sector and often supported the work from a technical perspective, handling a wide range of responsibilities including development, operations, and maintenance on my own.
Through my experience working in different welfare-related settings, I had opportunities to think about the work carried out in the field and how IT and the systems that support it can better meet those needs.

I have also tried to learn more about the issues facing society outside of my direct work experience.
In my free time, I attend study groups, events, and other gatherings related to areas such as DX and social welfare.
These experiences have helped me learn about issues that are actually being discussed in society and about the challenges that people and organizations face in practice.
They have also made me think about how I can make use of my own skills and experience to help address those challenges.

faq.question: What kind of engineer do you want to become?
faq.answer:
I want to build on my experience in development, operations, and maintenance while developing a stronger foundation in cybersecurity.

In my previous job, taking on many different responsibilities helped me develop my technical skills and strengthen my ability to solve problems independently.
At the same time, studying cybersecurity changed the way I looked at that experience.
I learned that even small organizations can become targets of cyberattacks.
This made me realize that relying too heavily on one person for technical knowledge and decision-making can create security risks as well as blind spots in judgment.
It can make it harder to notice gaps in knowledge or judgment, and it can also create security risks when there is no one else to review decisions or provide support.
While receiving employment transition support, I researched cybersecurity and organizational risk so that I could better explain my previous working style and current situation to my support staff.
We discussed what I had learned, and those conversations gave me an opportunity to look back on my past experience from a different perspective.
I came to understand how important it is for people to share their knowledge and experience, check each other's work, and support one another.
I also realized that relying on one person for a wide range of technical responsibilities can make it difficult to learn from people with different areas of expertise or to keep up with new technologies.
Because of this, I want my next role to be different from simply being the person who handles everything.
I want to work as part of a team where people can share their knowledge and experience and support each other.
I also want to develop a stronger area of expertise of my own.
In particular, I would like to deepen my knowledge of cybersecurity and become an engineer who can make a reliable technical contribution to the team.
I am currently studying cybersecurity and cloud technologies while taking care of my health and preparing for my next step in my career.
Building on the experience I have gained through web development, operations, and maintenance, I want to expand my expertise into areas that support the reliability and security of systems.

faq.question: What do you want to accomplish through technology?
faq.answer:
As technologies such as AI continue to advance, I want to think not only about the people who create and provide technology, but also about the people who use it and how it affects their lives.

DX is becoming part of more and more areas of society.
At the same time, I believe there are aspects of people's lives that technology cannot fully capture.
Individual experiences, emotions, and differences between people can easily be overlooked when we focus only on what digital technology can do.
I think this is especially important for companies whose systems and services are closely connected to people's everyday lives.
For companies whose technology plays a significant role in people's everyday lives, I believe it is especially important to understand the different needs and experiences of the people who use it.
I want to use the perspective I have gained from my own experiences to understand problems from both sides.
I want to think about the people who develop and provide technology, while also considering the people who use it.
I want to be an engineer who thinks about more than just technical safety.
I want to understand that different people may experience the same technology in different ways.
By paying attention to those differences, I hope to create technology that people can use with confidence and that genuinely meets their needs.
In the future, I want to combine my personal experiences with the technical skills I develop as an engineer.
As part of a Japanese company that values human connection, I want to contribute to improving social welfare in Japan through technology.
I want to approach this work with a genuine sense of personal responsibility because the people who use these services are not just users to me.
Their experiences are closely connected to the reasons I chose this path in the first place.

VisualThinking.text:
As part of exploring my personal roots, I have published a research article on the "Community of Mixed-Heritage Orphans in 1970s Nagoya and Its Cultural Evolution", a history my grandparents were closely involved in.

Given the sensitive nature of this topic, I approached the research with strict objectivity, prioritizing diverse viewpoints.
I gathered a wide range of sources, from rare books to international research papers, carefully cross-checking them to ensure historical accuracy.

Through this project, I learned to view individual events not as detached points, but as elements connected to a larger surface, mapping them within a broader social and structural context.
This structural thinking directly translate into my web development work today.
In my daily practice, I rely on official Google documentation and technical community insights to ensure reliable system operation, maintenance, and optimization.

At the same time, I love using creative medium as a language to express my inner state and connect deeply.
On my days off, drawing inspiration from zines and museum visits, I have worked on various projects, including image processing, digital art, video editing, and creative coding.
I am particularly drawn to spirituality and the inner world, continuously researching and reinterpreting.
